screen_html.probe: every tick reads the verb off the live adapter, never a version number (_html_verb): the public edit_message when inspect.signature shows a parameter named parse_mode (positional-or-keyword or keyword-only; **kwargs does not count), else the adapter's own coroutine _edit_text, else none. The HTML form goes through that verb (edit_message(chat, message_id, html, parse_mode='HTML') and its SendResult, or _edit_text(chat, message_id, html, 'HTML') which raises on refusal); on any refusal other than 'not modified' the same tick edits plain through the public edit_message. Plain succeeded right after HTML failed = the HTML form was refused: screen_format 'plain', the reason in html_error (the exception class, or 'edit_message: <error>'), HTML tried again after HTML_RETRY_TICKS (12). No verb at all = plain, html_error 'no HTML verb (edit_message without parse_mode, no _edit_text)'. The record names the verb that carries the HTML: html_verb 'edit_message' | '_edit_text' | null
screen_html.contract: TelegramAdapter.edit_message(self, chat_id, message_id, content, *, finalize=False, metadata=None) -> SendResult: no parse_mode on any engine known today; without finalize it calls _edit_text(chat_id, message_id, content), plain text. TelegramAdapter._edit_text(self, chat_id: str, message_id: str, text: str, parse_mode: Any = None) -> None: normalizes the ids, passes parse_mode to Bot.edit_message_text only when given, raises the PTB error on refusal ('Message is not modified' included). A PRIVATE method: the plugin treats it as a capability, never as a promise, asks the public verb's signature first (the catalog review's order) and keeps the plain public edit as the fallback. The parse mode is the string 'HTML' (ParseMode.HTML is that string); the markup is <b> and one <blockquote expandable>, both Bot API 7.4+, not the rich_message parameter

The text-to-speech 429: ERROR tools.tts_tool 'TTS generation failed (gemini): Gemini TTS API error (HTTP 429): <error.message>' with its traceback (tools/tts_tool.py:310-314, tools/tts_tool_providers.py:603), repeated within the same second by the executor's WARNING cut at 200 characters (agent/tool_executor.py:994) and the voice reply's WARNING (gateway/run_voice.py:342); the LLM path: WARNING agent.conversation_loop 'API call failed ... summary=Gemini HTTP 429 (RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED): ...' (agent/turn_recovery.py:916-919, agent/gemini_native_adapter.py:628); the streamed call: ERROR agent.chat_completion_helpers 'Streaming failed before delivery: Gemini HTTP 429 (RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED): ...' with its traceback (agent/chat_completion_helpers.py:3150), beside the turn loop's WARNING 'Retrying API call in Ns' (agent/turn_recovery.py:1091-1095), the engine's own backoff and not Google's retry. QuotaFailure and RetryInfo are dropped by the engine: only the message is logged. The last 429 is kept in the plugin record (gemini_log_cache); a retry over 120 s is the daily quota, an event until the reset; any other 429 marks the line for an hour; no network (gemini_log.py)

The stamp is converted with the process's own zone, so the hour repeated when summer time ends adds an hour to the age of a 429 from that hour. cron.probe: HERMES_HOME/cron/ is a directory and cron/jobs.json parses as an object with a jobs list; the ticker stamps (ticker_heartbeat, ticker_last_success, ticker_last_error) are read when present and the first token of each is a number, the epoch; no directory or no jobs.json = unsupported, a file that cannot be read or parsed = unknown with the reason, no stamps = no ticker verdict (a live ticker is never assumed)

the KIND of last_error and last_delivery_error in a word (cron_jobs.error_kind), never the text
the epoch in the first token of each ticker stamp; the kind of the error in ticker_last_error, never the text
never_reads: the text of last_error, last_delivery_error and ticker_last_error
cron.contract: cron/jobs.py: jobs.json written atomically (mkstemp + rename) with the outcome of the LAST run per job: last_status in the documented closed set ok | error | delivery_failed | blocked_config plus delivery_queued (cron/scheduler.py), last_error, last_delivery_error, failure_streak (agent failures in a row; delivery failures are not counted), state scheduled | paused | completed | running | error. The ticker writes ticker_heartbeat every loop (60 s), ticker_last_success on a loop without an exception, ticker_last_error with the epoch on its first line and the text after it. The thresholds are the engine's own (hermes cron status): a heartbeat older than three ticks plus slack, 200 s, is a dead ticker; a next_run_at more than 15 min in the past with a live ticker is a job that is not firing. The engine's error texts are reduced to the kind of the error in a word in the order of the engine's own health projection (agent/monitoring/cron_health.py: auth, rate limit, timeout, network), then the Telegram delivery answers and the ticker's own failures; a last_status literal the plugin does not know is named as it is and is never green. A failure a later ok run replaced in jobs.json stays in the details for two ticks (cron_cache.held). The layered order of the checks (ticker alive, record consistent, run recorded, delivery confirmed) follows itpartypattaya/hermes-cron's cron-doctor (MIT); no code is taken from it

the text of a send error
telegram_traffic.contract: Five private attributes of TelegramAdapter, read as attributes of the live object, never called (no method of the adapter is invoked). plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py: is_connected is self._running (the adapter was started), which says nothing about updates arriving or replies leaving; the adapter counts for itself: _updates_received_total grows with every update Telegram hands to getUpdates in the current polling generation (kept for hermes-agent#102260), _polling_generation and _polling_generation_started_monotonic reset on every reconnect, _polling_last_progress_monotonic is the last successful getUpdates round-trip, _send_path_degraded makes send() answer SendResult(success=False, error='send_path_degraded') until the generation proves progress, and _edit_text does not check it, so the dashboard's own edit can move while every reply fails. Verdicts: the send path degraded past a 120 s reconnect grace = no sends (critical); no polling progress for 300 s = stalled (critical); no update seen for longer than twice the longest gap of the last 7 days, at least 6 h and at most 48 h, and only after a first update was seen = quiet (warning); three or more failed sends in the last hour = an event. The counter is read once per tick, so 'last update seen' is the tick that saw it grow. A failed send is the engine's own ERROR line 'Failed to send Telegram message' in logs/errors.log; successes are not logged at that level, so the last successful send the plugin can vouch for is its own confirmed edit (Confirmed in the details).
